title: Research: source borrowing reduces fixed-cap echo work (no new kappa)
body:
When the external source can be borrowed inside recursion and restored at call exit, the known four-way additive echo fits into **three extra dirty rows**. At the same five-row total, complete leaf work falls **1,040 to 928 for 51 factors** and **1,248 to 1,088 for 56 factors**. Every inverse and restoration call is included.

**Status: scoped recursive-interface construction; no new kappa or selected-supplier adoption.** The source must be exclusively writable and unobserved until return. Exact additive children are required; the package includes a nonlinear helper-corruption witness despite reversible leaves.

The baseline is strengthened beyond PR1057: it admits four-way nodes whenever the protected source is an immediate port. A typed recurrence proves the optimum for both source contracts within the declared ordered arity-2/3/4 templates. Neither result is an unrestricted circuit or scratch minimum. PR1164's 1,088-call result is credited; this contribution attains it with one fewer dirty row and compares against the stronger same-cap protected baseline.

Only `research/mutable-source-port-borrowing/` is added. It includes the proof, exact certificate, separate min-plus/free-module/dense oracle, modular scalar/access backend, source pins, attribution and open questions. At n=51, both versions use 550 data bits; counted scalar/access commands fall 39,524 to 35,268 and data-head moves fall 51,240,320 to 48,673,408. These are explicit model counts, not a measured runtime claim. Planning, preparation, scalar bit costs, dispatch, routing and any host adapters are separately charged.

Reproduce with Python 3.12 and the standard library:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/mutable-source-port-borrowing
```

Expected: `PASS_MUTABLE_SOURCE_PORT_BORROWING`, `PASS_MUTABLE_PORT_PACKAGE relocation=1 corruptions=5`, and `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`.

Validation covers all 1,099 small ordered trees, 2,400 signed immediate-port cases, a separate full cost-table computation through 56, 2,376 literal modular basis/dirty cases, 1,024 exhaustive scalar dirty states, six 51/56-factor fixtures, eleven semantic controls, and five actual source/certificate/code corruption rejections. Registered Python 3.12, optimized read-only Python 3.14.6 relocation, all 20 repository workflow tests and selected baseline bindings pass. Full selected cold replay and hosted CI are separate, unclaimed checks.

Base: `ef5f39403610d231a0c27e8a6b4f08c10209bcd6`; OS assignment seed **51**. [Claim and overlap context](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1505). The final full snapshot covered 772 open PRs and 199 discussion records. Concurrent PR1499/1522/1523/1524 have different source/frame/connector interfaces and are distinguished in `OVERLAP.json`.

Credit Gareth Davidson / bitplane (PR1057 and PR1159), woklerx (PR1164), and the PR673/730/758/822/628 lineage. Exact predecessor heads and unchanged reference bytes are preserved. The general constant-register and echo principles are not claimed as new.

The direct all-role adapter remains noncontracting even at zero saving, and no compatible selected-supplier source interval has been identified. The selected frontier, supplier code, historical evidence, review ledger and `upstream/` remain unchanged.

Prepared for **Hanson Sun (@bbMisk)** with substantial **OpenAI Codex assistance** in derivation, both implementations, verification and prose. Both checkers were written in the same AI-assisted session; no independent human review or formal multiplication proof is claimed. New work is Apache-2.0.
